body: It might be worth adding a comment to explain why we're `lerp()`ing with a negative value (if contrast is positive), as this doesn't look very intuitive.

Done.

> if contrast is positive

It's positive in dark themes and negative in light themes by default, and some users don't use the default contrast sign in settings. Negative multiplier in that line pushes luminance in the opposite direction of regular luminance shift to make the lines visible against their background.

It's not as intuitive as a ternary at a glance, but it ensures that the value actually works with any editor settings.
